case.what_it_tests: Professional mode: detailed answer with section and page citations from BNSS
turns: Under the BNSS 2023, what are the conditions and procedure for granting anticipatory bail?

turns.input: Under the BNSS 2023, what are the conditions and procedure for granting anticipatory bail?

result.answer:
**Important notice:** Someone may be in police custody or may face arrest. This is a serious matter – you should get a lawyer right away. Free legal‑aid lawyers are available through NALSA 15100 or at the police station/court. --- ### How anticipatory bail works under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) | Point | What the law says (source) | |-------|----------------------------| | **Who can apply** | A person can seek anticipatory bail by filing an application under **Section 482 BNSS** in the High Court or the Court of Session (as shown in case practice). | | **When the court may grant bail** | **Section 485(1) BNSS** allows a High Court or Court of Session to direct that a person in custody be released on bail. | | **Conditions the court may impose** | • **Section 480(3) BNSS** – for offences punishable with imprisonment of 7 years or more (or offences listed in Chapters VI, VII, XVII of the BNS), the court must impose the following conditions:
 1. Appear before the court when required (as per the bail bond).
 2. Not commit any offence of a similar nature while bail is in force.
 3. Not tamper with, conceal or destroy evidence, nor induce any witness to withhold testimony.
• **Section 485(1) BNSS** – the court may also impose any other condition it considers necessary for the purposes mentioned in sub‑section (3) of Section 482. | | **When the mandatory conditions apply** | The mandatory conditions of Section 480(3) apply only if the offence is punishable with imprisonment of **seven years or more**, or if it falls under **Chapters VI, VII, or XVII** of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (LiveLaw article). They are **not** mandatory for all offences. | --- ### Practical steps a lawyer would take 1. **Draft the anticipatory bail petition** under **Section 482 BNSS**, stating why the applicant believes arrest is likely and describing the nature of the alleged offence. 2. **Cite the relevant provisions** – Section 482 for the right to apply, Section 485(1) for the court’s power to release on bail, and Section 480(3) for the mandatory conditions (if they apply). 3. **Argue that the applicant will comply** with any conditions the court may impose (e.g., appearing when required, not tampering with evidence). 4. **Request that the court impose only reasonable conditions**, pointing out that the mandatory conditions of Section 480(3) are limited to offences with imprisonment of 7 years or more. 5. **Be prepared to address any objections** from the prosecution, such as concerns about evidence tampering or witness intimidation, by showing the applicant’s willingness to cooperate with the investigation. --- ### What to do next - **Contact a lawyer immediately** – you can obtain a court‑appointed lawyer by calling **NALSA 15100**. - **If you are already in police custody**, ask for a free legal‑aid lawyer at the station. - **Keep a copy of this information** and share it with your counsel. --- **Sources** - LiveLaw article on **Section 480(3) BNSS** (mandatory bail conditions). - **Section 485(1) BNSS** – power of High Court/Court of Session to direct bail. - **Section 480(3) BNSS** – conditions for bail in serious offences. - **Section 482 BNSS** – special powers of High Court/Court of Session (used for anticipatory bail). *If any point is unclear or you need more detail, please consult a qualified lawyer.* ⚠️ Not found in the sources: Section 485(1) BNSS allows the court to impose any other condition it considers necessary for the purposes mentioned in sub-section (3) of Section 482.. Please double-check these points before acting on them.

claims.claim: Free legal-aid lawyers are available through NALSA 15100.
A person can seek anticipatory bail by filing an application under Section 482 BNSS.
Anticipatory bail applications under Section 482 BNSS are filed in the High Court or the Court of Session.
Section 485(1) BNSS allows a High Court or Court of Session to direct that a person in custody be released on bail.
Section 480(3) BNSS applies to offences punishable with imprisonment of 7 years or more.
Section 480(3) BNSS applies to offences listed in Chapters VI, VII, or XVII of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
Under Section 480(3) BNSS, the court must impose a condition that the accused appear before the court when required.
Under Section 480(3) BNSS, the court must impose a condition that the accused not commit any offence of a similar nature.
Under Section 480(3) BNSS, the court must impose a condition that the accused not tamper with, conceal or destroy evidence, nor induce any witness to withhold testimony.
Section 485(1) BNSS allows the court to impose any other condition it considers necessary for the purposes mentioned in sub-section (3) of Section 482.
The mandatory conditions of Section 480(3) BNSS are not mandatory for all offences.
